A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CorrGCV research and contain readable main text, equations, figures, and appendices A–K. Relocated material can be matched reliably across versions.

before.justification: v1 reports original synthetic ridge-regression experiments, including risk estimates and bias–variance decompositions. Appendix K describes repetitions over ten independently drawn datasets.

after.justification: v3 retains these original regression experiments and reports an expanded numerical minimum-eigenvalue comparison in Figure 6.

M1.justification: The ridge estimator, CorrGCV calculation, and correction for correlated test points are retained. Appendix A preserves the computational steps and code; reorganized deterministic equivalents do not introduce a new method.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same synthetic regression settings: exponential, nearest-neighbor, and power-law correlations, isotropic and structured features, noise mismatch, and correlated test points. Figure 6 varies matrix size within an existing scenario.

E2.justification: The evaluated comparators remain ordinary GCV, the Altman/Opsomer correction, and Carmack's GCCV in their corresponding comparisons. Newly cited ROTI-GCV is discussed as related work, not evaluated.

E3.justification: Figure 6 expands a single empirical eigenvalue comparison into a matrix-size comparison labeled n = 2, 4, and 2048. Its caption instead gives 1024 as the largest size, leaving that detail inconsistent. The regression protocols are retained.

E4.justification: Figure 6 extends the existing minimum-eigenvalue check to examine finite-size behavior relative to the infinite Toeplitz operator. The other bias–variance, double-descent, correlation-sensitivity, and forecasting-horizon analyses remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions report error bars over ten datasets and describe the same averaging procedures in Appendix K. The added deterministic matrix-size comparisons introduce no new uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: Figure 6 replaces the earlier single empirical series with size-specific eigenvalue results, retaining agreement with the positive asymptotic lower bound. The regression plots, comparator rankings, and corresponding findings are unchanged.

T1.justification: Appendix E.2 rewrites the proof of Proposition E.1 using explicit Toeplitz symbols and minimum-eigenvalue bounds, correcting the power-law symbol. The setup replaces mandatory unit diagonal with trace normalization, and Sections 3.1 and C.4 correct risk prefactors. The principal asymptotic results remain.

C1.justification: The conclusion narrows v1's characterization of kernel regression with correlated datapoints to ridge regression with correlated Gaussian datapoints, treating nonlinear and non-Gaussian extensions as expectations. The central CorrGCV and correlated-test claims are retained.

C2.justification: v3 explicitly states that Gaussian universality for non-independent data has not been rigorously established, sharpening v1's expectation that universality holds under weak conditions. Figure 6 also adds discussion of how closely small-matrix eigenvalues approximate the infinite-operator minimum.

D1.justification: Appendix A.2 clarifies fitting the empirical kernel to parametric correlations and estimating stationary lag autocorrelations using O(T) parameters. Appendix K resolves its earlier future-release wording, although v1 already supplied the same code link. The code listing and computing-resource information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v3 adds a substantive comparison with Luo et al. (2024), positioning their right-rotation-invariant, non-Gaussian setting as complementary. Additional citations support correlated Wishart equivalents and Toeplitz eigenvalue bounds; the overall research positioning remains.

P1.justification: The introduction integrates the former related-work subsection, setup becomes a separate section, and Section 2 is reorganized around weak, one-point, and two-point equivalents. Existing appendix formulas are brought into the main narrative, explanations are revised, and the contents page is removed.

P2.justification: The main text and references switch from single-column to two-column layout, with extensive figure relocation and appendix reflow. Several previously adjacent appendix figures occupy separate pages. Figure 6 is redrawn with a new legend, markers, axis presentation, and expanded caption.

improvement.justification: Corrected risk prefactors, a more explicit eigenvalue-bound argument, expanded finite-size checks, and clearer Gaussian-scope qualifications improve accuracy and assessability. These are limited gains around an unchanged core method and regression evidence. Figure 6's conflicting maximum-size labels remain a small reporting drawback.
